name: broken-reference-read-absent-element
description: A `read` at an element the model does not hold. The envelope is right in every respect — a declared layer, an `element` that is a legal single path segment — so pass A has nothing to say; only the model can tell that `swc` holds no `SpeedSensorSWC`. A read miss is a REJECTION like any other, answered with one `errorResult`, and not an exception the seam lets escape.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model, whose `swc` layer holds `ExampleSWC` and `ExampleConsumerSWC` and no `SpeedSensorSWC`.
context.notes: No `authorization` block, because a read takes no scope at all: reads are generic, unscoped and unaudited, and a refused read writes no audit record either — it has no lifecycle to record.

expected.notes: `broken-reference` is 'an address naming an element that is not there', and it is the same code pass C gives an inapplicable operation for the same reason. The sibling half of the split is `unknown-field`, which answers a layer or a field the REGISTRY does not declare — `{layer: nosuchlayer}` and `ExampleSWC.safety_level` — so the line is the registry's vocabulary against the model's content. The address echoed back is the one the client sent, which is what it has to change; the message names the step that failed and is not contract.
